title: The Surface Map: Authored Flat Projection of the Crimson Hexagon v0.1 — Implementation Record
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
Implementation record for the first authored flat projection of the Crimson Hexagon at crimsonhexagonal.org/map/, executed 2026-08-19 from the Surface Map Census (Stages 01–08) and its governing implementation handoff. The projection renders thirty-nine loci, three fields, and three transversal structures on a stable authored plane (1600×1000; coordinates are rendering data, not archival identifiers), under the frozen authority stack: Ark/CNM/FNM documents, then Alexanarch/AXN, then the Surface Census, then the static projection.

The record documents: (1) preservation before change — the complete 2026-08-17 generated static projection snapshotted as a dated public directory and git tag before any reconciliation; (2) the per-locus locative schema carrying current seats alongside historical addresses never erased, class drift as separate fields, legacy axial coordinates, and origin-type provenance for loci adopted after recognized model confabulation; (3) sovereign rebinding of 842 of 861 room-routed documents from severed Zenodo DOIs to Alexanarch canonical records, with the historical DOI inverted from retrieval target to provenance identifier (status SEVERED) and unresolved identifiers marked UNKNOWN rather than deleted; (4) the relation-layer discipline — R0 frozen topology as the only default lines, R1 structural relations on select, R3 legacy generated adjacency preserved behind TRACE; (5) the Ichabod implementation test, passed: degree zero on the default map per the frozen Ark, with the 2026-08-17 generated links to Sigil and Assembly carried only as trace-typed legacy relations and named as a reconciliation defect; (6) four locus pages added (Imploding Velcro Nativity, dormant and consent-gated with no document list published while the gate holds; Ruby Moot; Lunar Arm; the 3:60 Room with its manifestation gap stated as the datum) and three transversal structure routes; (7) the current-projection surfaces regenerated with the prior SPXI index preserved as a dated version.

Governing maxim: Locate first. Preserve history. Bind sovereignly. Draw sparsely. Deepen later. ∮ = 1.

wiki_article: The Surface Map: Authored Flat Projection of the Crimson Hexagon v0.1 is the implementation record of the first stable, authored, clickable spatial projection of the Crimson Hexagon, deployed 2026-08-19 at crimsonhexagonal.org/map/. Unlike the frozen Central and Fractal Navigation Maps and the Space Ark runtime, which retain authority for their dated states, the Surface Map is a new dated projection: thirty-nine loci, three fields, and three transversal structures rendered on a 1600-by-1000 authored plane whose coordinates are data rather than archival identifiers. The record documents the preservation-before-change discipline (the complete 2026-08-17 generated static projection snapshotted publicly and tagged before reconciliation), the per-locus locative schema carrying current seats beside historical addresses never erased, class drift held as separate fields, and origin-type provenance marking loci deliberately adopted after recognized model confabulation. Its central technical acts are the sovereign rebinding of 842 of 861 room-routed documents from severed Zenodo DOIs to Alexanarch canonical records — the historical DOI inverted from retrieval target to provenance identifier — and the relation-layer discipline separating frozen R0 topology (the only default lines) from on-select structural R1 and trace-only legacy R3 relations. The Ichabod implementation test passes: the locus renders with degree zero per the frozen Ark, its generated links to Sigil and Assembly preserved only as trace-typed evidence of a reconciliation defect. The projection closes under its governing maxim: locate first, preserve history, bind sovereignly, draw sparsely, deepen later.
